> Raw counts go into DESeq2. Never CPM, never logged. The method does its own
> normalisation and feeding it normalised data breaks it.
>
> Pi writes the code and you decide what it means. Ask it to use `d` and
> `metadata` from the setup chunk, and to put its code under the step you are
> working on.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

d <- read_counts("instructional")

# The grouping you built and saved in notebook 02. If it is not there yet, this
# stops with a clear message instead of a confusing one.
groups_file <- here("data/my_sample_groups.csv")
if (!file.exists(groups_file)) {
  stop("Could not find ", groups_file,
       "\nGo back to notebook 02, Exercise 2, step 5 and save your per-sample ",
       "table with the `community` column. Or rebuild it here: the Lactobacillus ",
       "fraction from the species table, split at 0.5.", call. = FALSE)
}
sample_groups <- read_csv(groups_file)

metadata <- d$metadata |> left_join(sample_groups, by = "sample_id")
```

```{r}
count(metadata, time_point, community)
```
